answer.text:
Bakery was descoped from the December 2025 fresh go-live: the go/no-go held on 17 November 2025 approved produce, dairy and chilled ready meals, and bakery was descoped to a separate workstream starting March 2026. The recorded reason is that bakery accuracy was poor because roughly half of bakery is baked in store, making it a production planning problem rather than an ordering problem. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

Scoping of the bakery workstream with Meridian began in January 2026, and the bakery interface points were agreed by early March 2026. In the 17 March 2026 design workshop the agreed boundary was that RELEX produces a day-level forecast plus a fixed intraday profile, Meridian consumes it and decides how it becomes a production plan, and RELEX does not produce an intraday forecast. [6] [7] [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]

Bakery build work is continuing: the 6 April 2026 weekly update lists 'Bakery build continues' as planned work for that week, and the March 2026 steering report states the bakery build is progressing. The weekly updates do not carry a bakery-specific 'on track' status beyond the overall project status. [13] [14]

Pending customer decision 1 - intraday profile ownership: the workshop left open who re-derives the fixed intraday profile when the shape changes and how often. Sofia Almeida offered that it would be her, but Nadia Haddad proposed not deciding that day and putting it on the open items list with no owner, which was accepted. [15] [16] [17] [18] [19] [20]

Pending customer decision 2 - intraday sales history: the intraday sales history sits in the till system, not in SAP. Priya Nair promised in the 17 March 2026 workshop to open the conversation with the owning team that month; the archive contains no confirmation that the conversation was opened or the data obtained. [21] [22]

Pending customer decision 3 - bakery expansion: an internal renewal and resourcing discussion on 2 July 2026 recorded an expansion conversation about bakery which Meridian is fronting, with RELEX subcontracting or partnering, and roughly two hundred additional stores if it lands. No decision or commitment is recorded in the archive. [23]

Pending customer decision 4 - chain-wide rollout: Robert Kahn asked on 17 June 2026 for a chain-wide number before the end of the month, because Acme's budget cycle starts in August and otherwise it would not happen until 2028. Marco Rossi sent indicative numbers on 26 June 2026 (approximately 420 thousand additional annual licence plus approximately 260 thousand one-off implementation for 340 stores), noting the value case depends on the shelf life data field that was identified as a dependency in April 2024 and never obtained. No final customer decision appears in the archive. [24] [25]

Pending decision 5 - bakery evidence review: Ana Duarte scheduled the bakery evidence review for Thursday 9 July 2026 at 10:00 Helsinki time, where she will prepare the comparison of prepared extracts versus a separate environment, including the earlier access decision and setup estimate, and Priya will bring updated Acme requirements. The earlier access decision remains in place pending that review. [26]

Related open item: the shelf life data field (warehouse data) remains unresolved. It was identified as a dependency in April 2024 and never obtained; a workaround built in September 2025 works acceptably on fast-moving articles and poorly on slow-moving ones, and the warehouse system owner is Nils Ackermann under logistics IT. This affects the chain-wide value case; the archive does not record a bakery-specific impact. [25] [27]

Recommendation: for the briefing, lead with the bakery integration status (descope decision, agreed interface, build progressing) and then list the five pending customer decisions above, marking clearly which are promises versus decisions: the intraday profile ownership is an open item with no owner, the till-system history conversation was promised but not confirmed, the bakery expansion and chain-wide rollout have no recorded commitment, and the evidence review on 9 July 2026 is the next scheduled decision point. [1] [2] [6] [11] [18] [22] [23] [24] [25] [26]

citations.quote:
Robert,

Indicative numbers attached. Summary here so you have it in the mail.

Chain wide for the three fresh categories, 340 stores: additional annual licence of
approximately 420 thousand, plus implementation of approximately 260 thousand one off.

On your second point, and this is the honest version.

The twelve month expectation was missed for one reason above all others. The value case
depended on fresh, and fresh depended on a data field that we identified as a dependency
in April 2024 and never obtained. Everything else largely went to plan. We built a
workaround in September 2025 which works acceptably on fast moving articles and poorly on
slow moving ones, and your category manager has been compensating for the difference by
hand ever since.

For the next number to be different, that field has to be available. It is not a RELEX
deliverable and I cannot commit to it on your behalf, which is why I am putting it in
writing rather than in a slide.

If it is not resolved, chain wide will reduce waste by less than the pilot suggests,
because the slow moving articles are a larger share of the tail across 340 stores than
across 25.
